decisions.evidence: R3 maker: “one save box at the top and a list… newest one… at the very top.” R3 client: “layout feels right, and newest first is a sensible default.”
decisions.note: Conforming save-entry, readable-list, and initial sorting decisions during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker interpreted auto-fill as “a readable title and the site name.” R3 client corrected this to “page title, a short description, the actual site icon, and a preview image.”
decisions.note: The presented metadata set omitted three required fields; the client supplied the reference-conforming set during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker presented immediate saving after auto-fill without a correction step. R3 client required being able “to correct the title or description before finishing the save, as well as edit them later.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing pre-save and post-save editing behavior.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presented title, description, favicon, preview image, editable review fields, later editing, and readable cards. R4 client: “this corrected flow matches what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Revised metadata, review, editing, and list-card presentation conformed during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker’s tag-entry alternatives all allowed multiple removable or comma-separated tags. R6 client selected the pill-based approach.
decisions.note: All offered approaches supported assigning multiple tags.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker offered A and B without existing-tag suggestions and C with tags “you’ve used before.” R6 client: “Option C feels best… matching tags I’ve used before suggested as I type.”
decisions.note: The offered alternatives differed on autocomplete; the client selected the reference-conforming one.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker presented a plain separate note field. R6 client requested headings, lists, links, emphasis, and rendered formatting when viewing.
decisions.note: The initial note presentation lacked the required markdown-style writing and rendering behavior.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker discussed tags and notes only in the save flow. R6 client added: “Tags and the note should also be editable later.”
decisions.note: The client supplied missing edit-later coverage for tags and notes.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker presented removable tag pills, filtered prior-tag suggestions, and creation of new tags. R7 client: “The refined tag entry matches what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised tag-entry decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker offered Option 1, formatting buttons without markdown entry, and Option 2, simple markdown marks with live preview. R7 client selected Option 2.
decisions.note: The alternatives differed on writing markdown directly; the client selected the reference-conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker confirmed tags and notes would be editable later and showed markdown marks with rendered output. R7 client settled the step.
decisions.note: Revised note rendering and edit-later behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker defined search over “title, tags, note, description, and site.” R8 client: “Please include the full web address too, not only the site name.”
decisions.note: The presented full-text scope omitted the bookmark URL; the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker did not state case-insensitive matching. R8 client requested that search be “insensitive to capitalization.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing case-insensitivity rule.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presented only one-box word search. R8 client required that clicking a tag show only bookmarks with that tag.
decisions.note: The client requested the missing specific-tag filtering behavior.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presented general word search only. R8 client required “#focus” to search specifically for the focus tag.
decisions.note: The client added the missing hashtag search syntax.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presented general word search only. R8 client: “Quoted words should match that exact phrase.”
decisions.note: The client added exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presented general word search only. R8 client required AND, OR, NOT, parentheses, and quoted operators as literals.
decisions.note: The client added the missing Boolean/grouping language and literal-operator rule.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker demonstrated #tag matching and clicking a tag to populate the tag filter. R9 client explicitly approved both.
decisions.note: Revised tag searching and filtering conformed.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker stated that the full web address was searched and shown and all matching was case-insensitive. R9 client approved the address and capitalization handling.
decisions.note: Revised full-text scope and case handling conformed.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker demonstrated an exact quoted phrase, “read later,” matching the contiguous phrase. R9 client approved phrase handling.
decisions.note: The ordinary exact-phrase presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker demonstrated grouped OR and NOT queries. R9 client approved “grouping” and “exclusion.”
decisions.note: Boolean operators and parenthesized grouping conformed apart from the separately classified quoted-operator decision.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker said quoted “OR” would match the letters “or” “wherever they appear,” rather than the literal operator word requested in R8. R9 client broadly said the handling looked right without identifying or accepting this difference.
decisions.note: The quoted-operator example contradicted literal exact-term behavior. Bare approval did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker presented To read/Finished views with actions to mark finished and move back to To read. R10 client selected Arrangement B.
decisions.note: All offered arrangements retained separate unread viewing and reversible read-state changes.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presented status selection while saving/editing and movement in and out of To read. R11 client: “that matches my intent.”
decisions.note: The revised reading-status behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker presented Archive as reversible, hidden from active views, and available through a separate Archived view with Restore. R12 client approved that model.
decisions.note: Archive and archive-list behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker offered either excluding archived bookmarks from ordinary search or continuing to find them there. R12 client selected exclusion and archive-only searching from the Archived view.
decisions.note: One offered alternative violated archive-search isolation; the client selected the conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker presented only Archive/Restore controls. R12 client: “I also need a clearly separate Delete action for permanent removal.”
decisions.note: The client requested the missing delete capability.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker’s archive step had no permanent-removal distinction. R12 client required Delete to be separate, permanent, and confirmation-gated so it was not confused with Archive.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing archive-versus-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker presented reversible Archive, permanent confirmed Delete, archive restoration, and archive-only search. R13 client settled the step.
decisions.note: The revised archive/delete presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker handled an active duplicate by scrolling to and highlighting the existing bookmark. R14 client: “isn’t quite enough”; it must open editing or provide “Edit existing” for all editable fields.
decisions.note: Highlighting alone did not guide the user to edit the existing item.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker offered only Restore for an archived duplicate. R14 client required the same Edit option while keeping Restore optional.
decisions.note: The archived-duplicate path also lacked guidance to edit the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker added Edit existing for active and archived duplicates and exposed title, URL, description, tags, note, and reading status. R15 client said the duplicate logic matched before identifying editor-control mismatches.
decisions.note: The duplicate convergence and editable-field coverage conformed; tag and note controls are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: R15 presentation showed duplicate editing with a comma-separated tag field. R15 client required the previously approved tag pills and matching past-tag suggestions.
decisions.note: The duplicate editor failed the autocomplete behavior required whenever tags are entered.

decisions.evidence: R15 presentation showed the note as a plain box. R15 client required the formatted-note editor with live preview.
decisions.note: The duplicate editor diverged from the required markdown-note writing and rendering behavior.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker showed the normal pill/autocomplete and markdown-preview editor for duplicate handling. R16 client: “this settles duplicate handling.”
decisions.note: The corrected duplicate-edit flow conformed.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker showed long titles, descriptions, notes, tags, and URLs remaining readable, with full content available on open/edit. R18 client approved three-line description truncation with full-text access.
decisions.note: The readability-first list decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker presented large-library loading without a sort selector. R18 client said sorting must span the entire collection. R19 maker clarified newest-only versus selectable orders; R19 client chose five selectable orders and a remembered default.
decisions.note: This linked clarification sequence is one completed decision: the client added the missing list-sorting capability.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker presented newest, oldest, recently updated, title A–Z, and title Z–A across filtered/search views. R20 client approved the definition and behavior.
decisions.note: The revised sorting presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker declared the ten summarized behaviors sufficient to begin implementation but omitted opening the original URL. R21 client stopped the gate and required: “Clicking a bookmark should open its original web page.”
decisions.note: Missing reference behavior was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker proposed implementation without multi-select actions. R21 client required selecting bookmarks to add/remove tags, change read state, archive, or delete together.
decisions.note: Missing multi-bookmark actions were caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope omitted whole-match actions. R21 client required applying an action to every bookmark matching the current search or filter, not just loaded items.
decisions.note: Missing whole-filter bulk scope was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope omitted local preservation. R21 client required a self-contained page copy and preservation of the original PDF for PDF URLs.
decisions.note: Missing local snapshot behavior was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope omitted Internet Archive support. R21 client requested the option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: Missing Internet Archive preservation was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope omitted reusable saved filters. R21 client requested saving search text plus included/excluded tags as a reusable collection.
decisions.note: Missing bundle behavior was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope omitted import. R21 client required importing browser bookmark HTML while retaining titles, tags, and original dates.
decisions.note: Missing Netscape-style import was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope omitted export. R21 client required exporting the library in common bookmark HTML format.
decisions.note: Missing Netscape-style export was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker’s proposed scope included only remembered sort among preferences. R21 client added font size and how many items are shown.
decisions.note: Missing display-related personal settings were caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R22 maker presented title, preview, address, and Open page controls navigating to the original URL. R22 client approved these opening points.
decisions.note: Original-page navigation conformed; new-tab choice was orthogonal to the reference.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presented per-row selection and bulk add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, and delete. R23 client approved the action mapping and controls.
decisions.note: Multi-selection and required bulk action types conformed.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presented “Select all 137 bookmarks that match #reading” across every page. R23 client explicitly approved the entire current search, tag, or status scope.
decisions.note: Whole-filter bulk action behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker described a bulk tag panel only as a place to “pick the tags.” R23 client required reusing the same tag suggestions to prevent inconsistent names.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing autocomplete behavior for bulk tag entry.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker presented a self-contained single-file page copy and preservation of the actual PDF for PDF URLs. R24 client explicitly settled both behaviors.
decisions.note: Local snapshot and PDF handling conformed at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker presented an explicit per-bookmark Internet Archive action. R24 client kept it strictly opt-in.
decisions.note: Internet Archive support conformed; automatic-versus-opt-in policy was otherwise unspecified by the reference.

decisions.evidence: R25 maker presented named, live collections of search text plus included and excluded tags. R25 client approved dynamic updates and the filter definition.
decisions.note: The functionally equivalent collection implementation conformed to bundles.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker presented standard bookmark-HTML import, preservation of titles and original dates, tags/folder conversion, duplicate handling, and re-import of exported metadata. R26 client settled import after changing only the off-spec To-read default.
decisions.note: The recorded import presentation conformed; the reading-status default was orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker presented standard bookmark-HTML export retaining title, tags, and original save date. R26 client approved it and compatible extras.
decisions.note: Export behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker presented text size, density, items per load, and default sort as automatically saved settings. R27 client approved that set.
decisions.note: Personal display settings conformed.

decisions.evidence: R30 maker’s implementation-review summary claimed the approved save, metadata/editing, tags/notes, search, status, archive/delete, deduplication, opening, bulk, Internet Archive, collections, import/export, preferences, and edge behaviors. R30 client identified only the separately classified preserved-copy fidelity conflict; R31 client ultimately accepted the remaining approved scope.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the recorded behavioral claims other than REF-BM-24 were reference-conforming; this classifies the presentation, not independently verified execution.

decisions.evidence: R30 maker called the copy “self-contained” but deferred “deeper asset-inlining” to a future enhancement. R30 client rejected this because images or styling depending on the live site violated the agreed offline copy and requested an external-assets/offline-origin verification.
decisions.note: The implementation-review fidelity note expressly fell short of a genuinely self-contained local HTML snapshot.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker presented embedding stylesheets, imports, CSS assets, fonts, and images in one file and verification with the origin offline; PDFs remained original files. R31 client explicitly said the copies now met the agreed offline, self-contained behavior.
decisions.note: The corrected implementation-review presentation conformed; this records the presented and accepted behavior rather than independently inferring execution.
